stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria on a complex cross-platform live preview feature. openspec needed first to elaborate requirements and define ACs; speckit then to harden for testability, iframe security, XSS, concurrent edits, and network failure edge cases. Spec is null and ACs are empty — not hand-curated, so full spec run is warranted.

agentContributions.notes: Openspec returned empty acceptance criteria, so all criteria above were created from scratch based on the story title '[GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS.' The feature was inferred to be a real-time preview mechanism in a CMS editor that renders content as the author edits it, covering GO, UP, and MX markets. Key areas covered: real-time sync (AC-1, AC-2), baseline rendering (AC-3), error handling (AC-4, AC-6), media handling (AC-5), UI toggle persistence (AC-7), unsaved changes guard (AC-8), accessibility (AC-9), locale/market specificity (AC-10), empty state (AC-11), concurrent editing conflict (AC-12), XSS security (AC-13), and slow-network UX (AC-14). CAVEAT: Without detailed requirements documents or file contents, these criteria are best-effort inferences. If the actual feature scope differs (e.g., the preview is a separate URL, or involves a different rendering pipeline), some criteria may need adjustment.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Pipeline breakdown: OpenSpec contributed zero value — empty notes, no ACs, no splits, acceptanceChanged=false. Speckit compensated by creating 14 ACs from scratch based solely on the story title, with an explicit caveat that these are 'best-effort inferences' without requirements documents. The intended sequential pipeline (openspec elaborates → speckit hardens) did not function; speckit did all the work with no source material to review. While the 14 ACs appear reasonably comprehensive (real-time sync, XSS, accessibility, concurrent editing, error handling, locale specificity), they lack requirements traceability and may not reflect true feature scope. Human review needed to validate inferred ACs against actual requirements and to investigate why OpenSpec produced no output.
